statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 8 of 100 in the low band, seventeen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty-three and a half hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; sixteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress rises two points to 63 in the elevated band on a materially worse overnight escalation record: Iranian authorities say a merchant vessel struck off Hengam and Qeshm islands at about 01:30 UTC killed one person and injured three, UKMTO separately reports a vessel struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the strait, a hardline Iranian newspaper called for retaliation against tankers across the Gulf and Gulf of Oman, and the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global supply off its route. Confidence is 86: every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour and both overnight strikes were confirmed from independent outlets, while the one missing evidence class remains a live price path that no venue can supply until the scheduled 22:00 UTC reopening.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in sixteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures failed mean reversion has almost no path to measure across this horizon. Second, the last observable session was orderly and two-way rather than one-way: the cash range spanned only 159.61 points, the close finished about 105 points below the session high, and VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84. Third, none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail is observed, because observing them requires a live tape. The overnight escalation is genuine and is therefore carried in Stress at 63 rather than in Tail, consistent with the repository definition that Stress describes a difficult but potentially recoverable environment. The narrow danger window runs from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday, where the scheduled restart could express an unpriced weekend as a gap into thin liquidity; those five slots carry conditional Tail of 24, 23, 22, 21 and 20 and map to WATCH.
headline: Thirty-three hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while Iranian authorities say a merchant vessel struck off Qeshm killed one person and injured three, UKMTO reports a separate vessel hit by a projectile inside the Strait of Hormuz, the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supply off its route, WTI sits at $100.05 and prediction markets price the 16 September FOMC near 79 to 80 per cent for a rate increase.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour rather than carried over. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against this macro backdrop. The front Nasdaq-100 futures contract was independently confirmed this hour at a last price of 29,387.00, up 0.86 per cent, and is shown as closed, which corroborates the halt from a second venue rather than from the cash index alone. Rates and oil are equally static: the Federal Reserve H.15 release still carries its 10 September observation at 4.00 per cent for the 3-month, 4.56 per cent for the 2-year, 4.95 per cent for the 10-year and 5.37 per cent for the 30-year, while WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent.

What changed in the last hour is the escalation record, and it changed for the worse. The two explosions reported off Qeshm Island in the previous assessment are now a confirmed strike with casualties: the Qeshm city governor, speaking on state television, said a merchant vessel was struck at about 01:30 UTC off the coasts of Hengam and Qeshm islands, killing one person and injuring three, and did not specify the origin of the strike, although some Iranian outlets attribute it to the United States. Separately, UKMTO reported early on Sunday that a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, with crew condition and damage not immediately known. A hardline Iranian newspaper called for retaliation against all tankers in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, warning of a historic supply shortage, and the U.S. president said on Saturday that Iran likely caused the aerial attack that disrupted the Saudi East-West pipeline. The structural picture behind those increments is unchanged: that pipeline, which had been moving 4 to 5 million barrels a day and represents 4 to 5 per cent of global supply, remains shut after a drone attack launched from Iraq's Maysan province, removing the principal bypass around Hormuz. The diplomatic channel narrowed rather than widened: a senior Iranian official said Monday's meeting in Oman is not expected to produce a signed Hormuz agreement, Bahrain said it will not attend, and Oman has not officially announced the meeting.

The reason this severity is held in Stress rather than Tail is that Tail measures a pathological price path. No such path exists to be measured: there is no live tape, no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme to hold. Prediction markets price a 25 basis point increase at the 16 September FOMC near 79 to 80 per cent, but that meeting, Wednesday's retail sales and Thursday's claims and housing starts all sit beyond this horizon and function as checkpoints rather than priced outcomes. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run and is not used: its payload is stamped 01:28 UTC, well beyond the 90-minute freshness bound, and it reports a partial collection, so the assessment rests entirely on independent primary-source research. One candidate source was discarded during verification because the link resolved to an unrelated 30 August incident rather than to this morning's strike, and only items confirmed by direct fetch are published. The scheduled 22:00 UTC restart is the one genuine structural checkpoint inside the horizon, and it is treated as a conditional watch-band window rather than as an observed event.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 06:00 UTC on 12 September to 05:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there almost throughout, reaching 7 only in the final slot, in normal mode across the window and tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 57 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53, 56 and 57 to 61 by the close of the window as attention turned to the restart and the weekend escalation reports accumulated. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 through the middle of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window revised a past opinion with later information.
outlookSummary: Sixteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's seventeenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 8 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It steps to 24 in the restart hour, the top of the watch band, then eases through 23, 22, 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, and falls back through 19 and 18 to 17 by the close of the horizon. Those five watch-band slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday, a wider window than the previous assessment carried because the overnight strikes near Qeshm and inside the strait leave more of the weekend record unpriced. Stress holds near 62 through the quiet Sunday stretch, then builds to a 68 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture and thin reopening liquidity, before decaying to 63 across the Asian session. Confidence declines from 86 to 80 as distance from the last verified print grows, then recovers to 86 once a live tape exists again. Mode stays normal through the closure, is treated as event/whipsaw for the first two restart hours, mixed while early flow is assumed to normalise, and normal again by the end of the horizon. Monday's meeting in Oman, Tuesday's Empire State index and Wednesday's retail sales and FOMC decision all sit at or beyond the edge of this horizon and are treated as checkpoints rather than as priced outcomes.
